observations: Files I read: the request JSON (with its first reading) and source/original.txt. I opened these images with Read and looked at them myself, in this order: workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-02.png, then workflow/storyboards/page-02.png, then workflow/review/page-01.png, review/page-02.png and review/page-03.png. Boundary pages: I viewed storyboards-unnumbered/page-01.png and page-03.png and the numbered PNGs. I did not render the SVGs, and I did not open the character sheets.

The script matches the source word for word: caption plus label 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic'; Ananya 'We can organise our clinic workflow here.'; Meera 'And our team can use tools suited to each staff role.' plus label 'WELBUK CARE for clinic staff'; Ananya 'One team. Better coordination.' Meera's 'And our team...' follows on from Ananya's 'our clinic workflow', and 'One team' closes the pair.

In the numbered storyboard only, the WELBUK CARE label covers the beat note '3 / Meera discovers Welbuk Care for staff'. That note is a guide overlay that does not appear in the unnumbered PNG or the preview, so this does not affect readers.

Unnumbered page-02.png: in the top tier the caption (top centre) comes before the teal WELBUK PRACTICE label (top right). In the middle row, Ananya's balloon (left panel) comes before Meera's balloon and then the WELBUK CARE label below it (right panel). In the bottom tier there is a single balloon. Left-to-right, top-to-bottom reading gives the intended order, and no balloon competes across a panel border.

First-reader point: the Panel A caption breaks the top border, and the WELBUK PRACTICE label touches the right border. Both also happen in review/page-02.png. They read as deliberate corner- and edge-docked boxes, and the text inside has clear margins, is not clipped and does not cover Ananya's face or the laptop. Acceptable.

First-reader point: the tiny Panel D tail covers the 'ananya' name label, so attribution could be unclear. In the art, the short tail touches Ananya's open, smiling mouth from the balloon's left edge. Meera stands at right with her mouth closed, so the line is clearly Ananya's.

First-reader point: the product labels float. In the art, WELBUK PRACTICE sits above the laptop setup screen Ananya is typing on, and WELBUK CARE sits just under Meera's raised staff phone. Each label is beside the device it names, and they read as product captions. Acceptable.

transitions.observation: Morning reception gives way to the evening office: the window shows sunset sky, and the caption says onboarding begins. This follows from Ananya's resolve in 01-3.
Same desk and same evening. From typing over her shoulder, the view moves to Ananya, hand at her chin, glancing up while thinking about roles. The laptop is still open.
Same office. Meera, standing by the desk with the open laptop behind her, holds up the staff phone. Her 'And our team...' extends Ananya's previous line.
The two-shot joins them. Ananya, seated at the open laptop, turns to Meera, who holds the phone at her side, and they share a smile as Ananya sums up.
Evening office gives way to a later morning at reception. The caption 'A later morning: ...' marks the time jump. The new QR stand and wall TV show that the clinic now runs with Welbuk.

readingReview.comparison: The first reading's order was caption, WELBUK PRACTICE, Ananya, Meera, WELBUK CARE, Ananya. That matches the intended [1,2], [1], [1,2], [1], and so does my scan. The first reader's concerns were the border-touching caption and label, the tiny Panel D tail and the floating labels. I judged each one against review/page-02.png above: the boxes are docked on purpose with their text intact, the tail goes to the open-mouthed Ananya, and each label sits beside its device. None is a skip or an ambiguity in the accepted page.
